Using the PMO governance hub

How to report a risk or issue, ask for something to go to the Executive Board, and raise a change to the baseline. It also covers what happens next and what the colours on the hub mean.

Report a risk or issue

A risk might happen; an issue is happening now. The Master RAID Log also holds assumptions and dependencies (Risk, Assumption, Issue, Dependency).

  1. Select Report a risk or issue (also on the hub's quick links).
  2. Give it a short, specific title: what could go wrong, or what has gone wrong.
  3. Choose the type and the workstream. In Description, say what is happening and the impact on time, cost, scope or benefits.
  4. Set the RAG rating (table below), the owner who will manage it, and a target resolution date.
  5. Write the mitigation / resolution plan: what will be done, by whom, by when.
  6. Save. It shows in the RAID log straight away and is part of the weekly early-warning check.
RatingUse it when
RedA milestone, the budget or a benefit will be missed unless someone outside the workstream acts. Needs a decision or help now.
AmberAt risk, but the workstream has a credible plan to recover within its own authority. Watch closely.
GreenOn track, or the risk is fully mitigated.
UnassignedNot rated yet. Rate every open item; unrated items can't be prioritised.

Ask for Executive Board escalation

Escalate when the item needs a decision or help above the workstream's authority, for example funding, resources from another area, a supplier problem or a change of scope. Board escalation isn't a way to make an item look more urgent.

  1. On the RAID item (new or existing), tick Request Executive Board escalation.
  2. Fill in Why it needs the Board: what the Board must decide or unblock, and by when.
  3. Save. The Head of PMO gets an approval request with the details.
  • Within 5 minutesEscalation status: Requested
  • Within 3 daysThe Head of PMO approves or declines
  • If approvedApproved The item is flagged, shows on the hub and goes to the Steering Committee channel
  • If declined or no decisionDeclined or Not decided The tick is cleared; you can ask again

You and the item's owner get an email with the outcome and any comments. Once escalated, the item appears in the Steering Committee's daily digest if it passes its target date.

Raise a change request

Raise a change request (CR) to change the approved baseline: scope, budget or timeline (Scope, Budget, Timeline, Multiple). Don't move baseline dates or budget until the CR is approved.

  1. Select Raise a change request.
  2. Describe the change requested and the justification, and choose the workstream and change type.
  3. Enter the budget impact (GBP; negative for a saving) and the schedule impact in days, and summarise the impact on the baseline.
  4. Leave the CR reference blank: it is given a number (CR-nnn) automatically.

Who decides

The changeDecided byTime to decide
Budget impact up to £25,000 either way, schedule impact up to 10 days, and not a scope changePMO14 days
Any scope change, budget impact over £25,000, or schedule impact over 10 daysPMO review, then the Steering Committee14 days, then 21 days

What the status means

StatusMeaning
Under review - PMOThe PMO is checking it is complete and correct.
Under review - Steering CommitteeThe PMO supports it; it is with the Steering Committee.
ApprovedApproved. The PMO updates the baseline. The decision is logged in the Action and Decision Tracker.
RejectedNot approved. The baseline doesn't change.
Returned to requesterThe PMO needs more or different information. Raise it again as a new request.
Decision overdueNo decision in time. The PMO takes it to the next Steering Committee and records the outcome.
WithdrawnYou withdrew it. Set Status to Withdrawn at any time before the decision.

Moving a target or due date

Every time a RAID target date or an action due date is moved later, the change is recorded: the old and new dates, how far it moved and who moved it. The first date an item ever had is kept as its original baseline date. Bringing a date forward isn't counted.

Why it matters: an item pushed 2 or more times in 14 days is a sign the forecast isn't stable, and flags its workstream in the weekly early-warning check. When you move a date, say why in the mitigation or outcome, and quote the CR reference if a change request approved it.

What the PMO and the Board see

Daily overdue digest: weekdays at 07:00

The Steering Committee channel gets one card listing Board-escalated RAID items past their target date and Executive Board actions and decisions past their due date. Nothing is posted when nothing is overdue.

Weekly early warning: Mondays at 06:00

Each active workstream is checked for three warning signs: risks and issues opening faster than they close, actions closing too slowly against what is due, and dates being pushed repeatedly. A workstream with 2 or more signs gets an advisory in the PMO Risk Advisory channel with the reasons. Details are in the governance reference.

Executive escalations and decisions on the hub

The hub shows open Board escalations, decisions the Executive Board owes, the next 30 days of governance meetings, the latest PIDs and charters, change requests in progress and escalation requests waiting for the Head of PMO.

Help

For anything about the RAID log, escalations or change requests, contact the PMO through the PMO shared mailbox. The standard delivery framework, stage-gate guidance and templates are in Governance Framework & SOPs.
